description: Checks a glaze recipe for what is past a recommended limit for its firing (too much boron or alkali, too little alumina, too little or too much clay, rising expansion...) and says what the fired glaze will likely do, as the Glazecalc app does. A cone is checked in the band the recipe page gives it (low cone 06-02, mid 1-7, high 8-11); from cone 12 up (band 'top') no published limits reach, so the band's limits are not checked and limitsNote says so. With a firing, coneFit says whether the chemistry looks like that firing's, by Katz's boron rule and Hesselberth & Roy's silica and alumina whatever limit set is chosen: verdict 'cooler' or 'hotter' only when boron and silica or alumina agree on another band; 'fits' (nothing points away, not a pass); 'skipped' where the published figures do not reach (lead, lithium, much soda and potash or zinc, raku, cones 01 to 3, cooler than cone 06 or hotter than cone 10...). Cone 6 against cone 10 is told apart only roughly (strength 'soft'). stull says where the recipe sits on Stull's chart, as analyze_recipe gives it. These are cautions and guides from published figures, not a test and not a guarantee of food safety.

firing.description: The firing, as a cone or a temperature. Leave it out when it is not known. From cone 12 up (about 1320 °C) no published glaze limits reach, so the limits are not checked there; the cone check judges cone 06 to 10 only.

chart.description: Which cones the cone is: Orton (the default) or SK (JIS R 8101).

cone.description: An Orton cone from 022 to 42 ("06", "6", "10", "14", a half cone as "5.5"), or with chart "sk" an SK cone (JIS R 8101) from SK 022 to SK 20 ("6a", "8", "14").

language.description: The language for any sentences in the answer, as a BCP 47 tag such as "en", "de" or "ja". Languages Glazecalc does not offer are answered in English.

limitSet.description: The limits to check against: "glazecalc" or "hesselberth-roy" (Hesselberth & Roy, cone 6 and 10 only, no low-fire figures). Neither has figures from cone 12 up. Left out: the limit set saved in the account’s settings when the token may read preferences (the recipe page’s own, "hesselberth-roy" until changed), else "glazecalc".

lines.description: The recipe's base materials (not colorants), at most 40 lines.

amount.description: Its amount in the recipe, in any unit the other lines share (grams, parts, percent).

analysis.description: Only for a material not in the library: its oxides in weight percent, as { "SiO2": 68.5, "Al2O3": 17.4 }.

loi.description: Its loss on ignition in percent, with an analysis.

material.description: The material, by its name in the Glazecalc library ("Custer Spar", "Whiting", "EPK"), or your own name when you give its analysis.

name: check_limits
title: Check a recipe against limits
